method: Structured JSON from the Gemini API, instructed by docs/PROJECT_VISION.md@main blob fe2f414774b7. Every cited URL was fetched; dead links and pages that never mention the character were removed, and feats, results, conditions and campaign tags that lost their source were moved to unknowns. All records provisional.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Black Panther, Avengers: Infinity War, Avengers: Endgame, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
characters.summary: Okoye is the general of the Dora Milaje and Wakanda's foremost warrior, a master martial artist and spear expert who fights with a collapsible vibranium spear and Kimoyo Beads. After losing her rank in Wakanda Forever she wears Shuri's Midnight Angel armor, which grants superhuman physical attributes and thruster flight.

techniques: Collapsible vibranium spear thrusts and throws (thrown through an SUV windshield in Busan)

mechanisms: Master martial artist's evasion and parrying
Midnight Angel armor (Wakanda Forever): superhuman durability

weaknesses: Peak-human durability only when not wearing the Midnight Angel armor
Was disarmed of her spear and thrown off a bridge by Attuma in their first fight
mobility: Thruster flight while wearing the Midnight Angel armor
limitations: No innate superpowers; superhuman strength, speed, durability and flight come only from the Midnight Angel armor.

sources.supports: Dora Milaje general; collapsible electrified vibranium spear; Kimoyo Beads; Busan casino chase; Battle of Wakanda fight with Proxima Midnight; Midnight Angel armor powers and flight; two fights with Attuma and their outcomes.

feats.claim: Threw her vibranium spear through an SUV's windshield, lodging it in the road, during the Busan casino chase after taking down several bodyguards.
With Black Widow, held off Proxima Midnight during the Battle of Wakanda until Wanda Maximoff threw Proxima into a Thresher.
Threw Attuma off the Sea Leopard into the water while fighting as a Midnight Angel.

notableResults.note: Okoye and Black Widow held Proxima off during the Battle of Wakanda; Wanda Maximoff killed her by lifting her into a Thresher's path.
First fight in Cambridge: Attuma took her spear and, despite a Kimoyo Bead shock, threw her off a bridge.
Rematch aboard the Sea Leopard while wearing the Midnight Angel armor; she threw him off the ship into the water.

conditional.ability: Superhuman strength, durability, speed, agility, stamina and reflexes, plus thruster flight
conditional.dependsOn: Wearing the Midnight Angel armor built by Shuri

campaignTags.claim: Uses an electrified collapsible vibranium spear and Kimoyo Beads (shocked Attuma with one; tossed a remote-access bead onto a car in the Klaue chase).
The Midnight Angel armor gives her superhuman strength, durability, speed, agility, stamina and reflexes.
The Midnight Angel armor provides flight via thrusters.

unknowns: The MCU wiki does not place Okoye at the Battle of Edinburgh; the original Edinburgh claim was removed.
Original claim of vibranium rings and an energy staff could not be verified on the MCU wiki page.
Exact limits of her Kimoyo Beads' combat capabilities.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Captain America: The First Avenger, Agent Carter (TV series)
characters.summary: Peggy Carter is an SSR agent and trained fighter who uses firearms and hand-to-hand combat; she later helped Howard Stark found S.H.I.E.L.D. and co-headed it. She has no superhuman abilities.

techniques: Pistol and rifle marksmanship (including a tranquilizer rifle)

weaknesses: Normal human durability and physiological limits

sources.supports: SSR agent; Zodiac retrieval fight against guards; 1945 SSR raid on Hydra's last base; co-head of the newly founded S.H.I.E.L.D.

Shooting Heinz Kruger's driver; firing on a Hydra soldier's fuel tank to protect Steve Rogers; subduing Zodiac guards; defeating Dottie Underwood; tranquilizer rifle use; helping Stark found S.H.I.E.L.D.

feats.claim: During the attack on Hydra's last base, protected Steve Rogers by shooting a Hydra soldier's fuel tank, killing him.
Went alone to recover the Zodiac serum and fought off multiple guards, throwing one through a window.
Shot Heinz Kruger's getaway driver while pursuing him through Brooklyn.

notableResults.note: Ducked a swing and kicked Underwood through a window; in another clash knocked her out with a bag of money.

unknowns: Full extent of her capability against enhanced beings without preparation.
Original generic 'Hydra Soldiers' result removed: not a named opponent.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Iron Man films, Avengers: Endgame
characters.summary: Pepper Potts is Stark Industries' CEO. In Avengers: Endgame she fights in the Battle of Earth wearing the Rescue armor (Mark XLIX), which gives her flight, repulsor blasts and durability. In Iron Man 3 she was temporarily empowered by Extremis and used it to kill Aldrich Killian.

techniques: Repulsor blasts from the Rescue armor
Aerial strikes on Necrocraft and Thanos's forces

mechanisms: Rescue armor (Mark XLIX) resisting kinetic impacts and energy blasts

weaknesses: Ordinary human durability when not wearing the Rescue armor
No prior battlefield experience before the Battle of Earth
mobility: Powered flight via the Rescue armor's repulsors
limitations: Combat capability depends on the Rescue armor; her Extremis powers were removed by Tony Stark after Iron Man 3.

sources.supports: Arrives in her own armored suit to battle Thanos's army in Endgame; survives via Extremis and ambushes Aldrich Killian in Iron Man 3.
Rescue armor (Mark XLIX) flight, repulsors, HUD and durability; Battle of Earth actions; Extremis powers and their removal; killing Killian on the Norco.

feats.claim: Fought Thanos's forces from the air in the Battle of Earth, destroying Necrocraft alongside Iron Man and helping Captain Marvel through a horde.
With Shuri and the Wasp, blasted Thanos away when he tried to stop Captain Marvel.
Killed Aldrich Killian by kicking an explosive toward him and detonating it with a repulsor taken from an armor.

notableResults.note: Team result in the Battle of Earth; the army was wiped out by Iron Man's use of the Infinity Stones.
While empowered by Extremis, ambushed and killed Killian after he shrugged off Stark's missile attack.

conditional.ability: Flight, repulsor blasts and resistance to kinetic and energy attacks
Enhanced strength and agility, regenerative healing and intense heat generation
conditional.dependsOn: Extremis infection (Iron Man 3 only; later removed by Tony Stark)

campaignTags.claim: Wears the Rescue armor (Mark XLIX), giving flight, repulsors and superhuman durability.
Flies via the Rescue armor's repulsors in the Battle of Earth.

unknowns: Original claim of energy shielding systems in the Rescue armor was not supported by the sources and was removed.
Duration of the armor's power supply.

characters.summary: Phastos is the Eternals' inventor, an immortal who manipulates cosmic energy to create inventions and weapons and has technopathy. He guided humanity's technological revolutions, built the bracelets that formed the Uni-Mind, and briefly restrained Ikaris during the Emergence.

techniques: Cosmic-energy creation of devices and weapons (including a whip-like weapon used to drag Ikaris down)
Containment devices that suppressed Ikaris's powers

mechanisms: Eternal physiology (survived a direct hit from Ikaris's optic beams)
Celestial armor that withstood multiple Deviant blows

weaknesses: Not established beyond being injured by Thena during her Mahd Wy'ry episode
mobility: Levitated a few feet above the ground while forming the Uni-Mind
limitations: No sustained flight documented; his only flight-like feat is brief levitation during the Uni-Mind.

sources.supports: Technopathy; creating inventions and weapons from cosmic energy; durability against Ikaris's optic beams; whip-like weapon; containing Ikaris; Celestial armor; immortality; levitation during the Uni-Mind.
Phastos's inventor role; making the Uni-Mind bracelets; restraining Ikaris, who breaks free and flies off; knocking Kro away.

feats.claim: Restrained Ikaris and prevented him from using his powers momentarily during the battle at the Emergence.
Survived being shot directly by Ikaris's optic beams.
Built bracelets from Sersi's communication sphere that let the Eternals form the Uni-Mind.

notableResults.note: Phastos contained Ikaris and suppressed his powers for a time, but Ikaris broke free and flew off to stop Sersi.

campaignTags.claim: The Eternals' inventor; creates inventions and weapons from cosmic energy and built the Uni-Mind bracelets.

unknowns: Energy blast, force-field and holographic projection abilities are listed on the MCU wiki as 'to be added'; not verified.
Original claim that Ikaris subdued him could not be verified; result changed to inconclusive.
Limits of the scale of matter and energy he can construct at once.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Iron Man films, Thor, The Avengers, Captain Marvel, Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
characters.summary: Phil Coulson is a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who was killed by Loki in The Avengers, revived with Kree blood, and later became Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. He relies on firearms, S.H.I.E.L.D. technology and leadership, and briefly became a Ghost Rider to defeat AIDA.

mechanisms: Not established beyond standard tactical cover

weaknesses: Vulnerable to illusion-based deception (Loki stabbed him from behind using an illusion)
limitations: Normal human endurance and vulnerability to lethal trauma; Ghost Rider powers were a brief, one-time deal.

sources.supports: Stabbed through the heart by Loki in The Avengers; Project T.A.H.I.T.I.; made Director of S.H.I.E.L.D.; defeated a faction of Inhumans and lost a hand; prosthetic hand; became a Ghost Rider to defeat AIDA; Lola.
Coulson confronted Loki with the Destroyer gun, was stabbed from behind via illusion, and fired one shot that severely hurt Loki.

feats.claim: After being stabbed by Loki, fired the Destroyer-based prototype gun and severely hurt him, though Loki still escaped the Helicarrier.
As Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., led his team to defeat a faction of Inhumans, losing a hand in the process.

notableResults.note: Loki used an illusion to stab Coulson from behind with the Scepter; Coulson's dying shot hurt Loki but did not stop his escape.
Coulson briefly became a Ghost Rider to defeat AIDA.

conditional.dependsOn: A brief deal with a demon (Spirit of Vengeance) to become a Ghost Rider

campaignTags.claim: Uses S.H.I.E.L.D. technology including the Destroyer-based prototype gun, a prosthetic hand and Lola, his flying car.

unknowns: The 'Night-Night' pistol / ICER was not mentioned on the opened pages and was removed from techniques.
Original claim of S.H.I.E.L.D. body armor was not supported.
Long-term physical effects following his revival via Project T.A.H.I.T.I.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, Earth-838 (Illuminati): Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
characters.summary: The Earth-838 Charles Xavier is a telepathic mutant and member of the Illuminati who uses a yellow hover chair. During the Scarlet Witch's attack he telepathically entered Wanda Maximoff's mind to free her Earth-838 counterpart, but the Scarlet Witch killed him there.

mechanisms: Not established on the opened sources

weaknesses: Physically frail and dependent on a hover chair
Within a target's mindscape, a stronger mind can attack and kill him (as the Scarlet Witch did)

sources.supports: Xavier used telepathy to enter Wanda Maximoff's mindscape, found her Earth-838 self trapped in rubble, and was killed there by the Scarlet Witch.
Earth-838 Xavier as a mutant mind-reader recruited to the Illuminati; yellow hover chair; entering Wanda's mind to break her control over her Earth-838 counterpart; his death.

feats.claim: Telepathically entered the Scarlet Witch's mind and reached her trapped Earth-838 counterpart in an attempt to break her control.
feats.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
notableResults.note: Killed inside Wanda's mindscape after the Earth-838 Wanda was dragged away from him; the MCU wiki is inconsistent on whether she ripped his head off or twisted his neck.

campaignTags.claim: Mutant mind-reader who telepathically entered Wanda Maximoff's mindscape.

unknowns: Mind control and mental paralysis were not shown for the MCU Earth-838 Xavier on the opened sources; removed (likely comics or Fox film leakage).
Original Wikipedia source (Professor X in other media) could not be opened; replaced.
Upper boundary of his telepathic reach.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Black Widow, Thunderbolts*
characters.summary: Alexei Shostakov, the Red Guardian, is the Soviet super-soldier counterpart to Captain America, a strong and durable hand-to-hand brawler who served as 'the muscle' alongside Melina Vostokoff. Years in prison left him out of shape, but he remains capable of superhuman feats.

techniques: Shield throws (used Taskmaster's shield to kill one of Dreykov's men through a windshield)

mechanisms: Super-soldier durability (survived a fall in the prison courtyard; needed over a dozen tranquilizer darts to be knocked out)

weaknesses: Was beaten by Taskmaster in hand-to-hand combat
Out of shape after years in prison
limitations: Considerable weight gain and stunted conditioning from imprisonment; could not break out of the Red Room's containment cells.

sources.supports: Super-soldier strength and durability feats; prison fight and escape; Taskmaster fight outcome; shield use; uniform; weight gain in prison.

feats.claim: Broke the inmate Ursa's wrist, pulled a guard through a glass window with one arm and knocked down a large steel door during his prison escape.
Shrugged off one tranquilizer dart and needed more than a dozen to be knocked out.

notableResults.note: Fought well but was beaten; Melina Vostokoff intervened to save him from being killed.
Broke Ursa's wrist in prison after Ursa questioned his story.

unknowns: Thunderbolts* fights and feats are not covered on the opened page.
Original claim that he lifted tons of rubble could not be verified and was removed.
Exact chemical formulation compared to Steve Rogers' serum.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Captain America: The First Avenger, Avengers: Infinity War, Avengers: Endgame
characters.summary: Johann Schmidt, the Red Skull, is Hydra's leader, enhanced by an early super-soldier serum with great strength, speed, stamina, reflexes and intellect. He fights with a Tesseract-powered Luger-style handgun and studied mythical artifacts as science. After the Tesseract transported him to Vormir he became the Soul Stone's Stonekeeper.
weaknesses: Handling the Tesseract directly ended his campaign: it opened a portal and launched him to Vormir
limitations: Energy attacks depend on Tesseract-powered weaponry; his own enhancements are physical.

sources.supports: Serum-granted strength, speed, stamina, reflexes and intellect; punches that dented Captain America's shield; Tesseract-powered handgun and Luger; Tesseract portal to Vormir; Stonekeeper role; approach to mythical artifacts.

feats.claim: Punches strong enough to dent Captain America's original metal shield.

notableResults.note: Their fight ended when the Tesseract opened a portal and launched Schmidt into it, sending him to Vormir; he was removed by the Tesseract rather than beaten down.

unknowns: Original claim of tactical armor was not supported and was removed.
Full extent of his abilities as the Stonekeeper on Vormir.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Guardians of the Galaxy films, Avengers: Infinity War, Avengers: Endgame
characters.summary: Rocket is a raccoon enhanced by the High Evolutionary's experiments with intelligence and speech. He is an engineer who builds weapons and traps from scrap, an expert marksman and a skilled pilot of the Milano, Warbird and other ships.

techniques: Hadron Enforcer, laser cannon and blaster rifle fire
Traps: anti-gravity mines, electric head disks and needle traps
Ship ramming (crashed the Warbird into the Dark Aster)

weaknesses: Small stature; was overpowered hand-to-hand by Ravagers once his traps were exhausted
mobility: Starship piloting (Milano, Warbird, M-Ship, Quadrant, Benatar)
limitations: Relies heavily on manufactured weaponry and gear.

sources.supports: High Evolutionary enhancement; engineering and weapon-building; Hadron Enforcer and gadgets; piloting; Battle of Xandar; Berhert traps and capture; Battle of Wakanda; Battle of Earth.

feats.claim: His mines, disks and needle traps incapacitated a Ravager squad on Berhert, the electrical traps killing those they targeted.
Crashed the Warbird into the Dark Aster's breach during the Battle of Xandar, badly damaging both ships.
Fought Outriders alongside the Winter Soldier in the Battle of Wakanda.

notableResults.note: Team result in the Battle of Xandar; Rocket destroyed incoming ships and rammed the Dark Aster.
His traps took down many Ravagers on Berhert, but he was overpowered, Yondu's arrow forced his surrender, and Nebula shot him; he woke imprisoned on the Eclector.

campaignTags.claim: Uses anti-gravity mines, electric head disks, needle traps and Anulax Battery bombs.
Flew the Milano, Warbird and an M-Ship during the Battle of Xandar and piloted through an asteroid field escaping the Sovereign fleet.
Builds weapons such as the Hadron Enforcer from scrap and helped Tony Stark build a Quantum Tunnel.

unknowns: Original claim of armored combat suits was not supported (the page mentions only an Aero-Rig and Holographic Space Suit he gave to Yondu) and was removed.
Original claim of fighting Kree and Chitauri armies was not supported; fights with Sakaarans, Ravagers and Outriders are documented.
Exact durability limits of his modified body.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616): Guardians of the Galaxy, Captain Marvel
characters.summary: Ronan the Accuser is a radical Kree warlord of great strength and durability who wields the Universal Weapon, a war hammer that fires concussive force. He embedded the Power Stone in it, destroying the Nova Corps fleet, before the Guardians turned the Stone against him.

techniques: Concussive force blasts from the Universal Weapon

mechanisms: Superhuman Kree durability (shrugged off Drax's punches)
Kree armor that boosts strength and durability (withstood a Hadron Enforcer blast)

weaknesses: Once the Power Stone left his control, the Guardians turned its energy against him
limitations: His Stone-level power depended on the Power Stone embedded in the Universal Weapon.

sources.supports: Strength and durability; Universal Weapon and Kree armor; killing the Other; merging the Power Stone into the Universal Weapon; beating Drax on Knowhere; destroying the Nova Corps fleet; death at the Guardians' hands; retreat from Captain Marvel; surviving the Hadron Enforcer.

feats.claim: Broke the Other's neck with a blast of force from the Universal Weapon.
With the Power Stone in the Universal Weapon, destroyed the entire Nova Corps fleet with one blast.
Took a Hadron Enforcer shot to the chest and was only knocked off his feet.

notableResults.note: On Knowhere, overpowered Drax, tossed him around and left him to drown in a vat of spinal fluid.
Destroyed when Quill caught the Power Stone and the Guardians jointly turned its energy on him.

conditional.ability: Fleet-destroying blasts and increased strength and durability
conditional.dependsOn: The Power Stone embedded in the Universal Weapon

unknowns: Flight or floating was not documented for Ronan; the natural-flight tag and flight mobility were removed.
Original limitation that he cannot handle an Infinity Stone without a conduit was not verified; the MCU wiki says he briefly held the Power Stone's energy.
Full potential of the Universal Weapon with other Infinity Stones.
